This game is easily one of the best games in history. You take on the role of Gordon Freeman, a scientist with a PHD in theoretical physics at another average day at work at the underground Black Mesa reserach facility in New Mexico. The NPCs you meet along the way inform you that you are going to be participating in an experiment involving a specimen from an alien planet that is more unstable than anything they've seen so far, yet they ironically inform you that everything is going to be fine. But, it goes horribly wrong, opening up an interdimensional seam in which aliens from Xen (alien planet) start invading the facility and Earth. Before you know it the military is sent to cover the incident via killing everyone in order to prevent them from "talking".
You find yourself traversing through all sorts of areas including the in-ruins Black Mesa facility, deserts, military bases. and even Xen, while under the constant threat of multiple different kinds of aliens, and the military. One of the things that make this game so good is that you feel like you are actually Gordon Freeman, as opposed to feeling like you're just playing as somone. You never say one word throughout the game and there are no cutscenes, meaning that you are always in a first person point of view, you never once go to a third person point of view (cutscenes, dialogue etc.) Instead of story telling through cutscenes, the game tells the story through interaction, interaction with NPCs and other things. There's even a part where you get knocked out by the military and are being dragged away, and even then you are still in first person view.
Another thing that makes the game so immersive is going through the facility and witnessing the deaths of your fellow colleagues, by aliens, by falling to their deaths, or getting shot by the military. You name it, this provides a sense of fright and a sense of "Holy Crap".
You are armed with a vast variety of weapons in this game, which you aquire one by one progressively while playing the game, they range from assault rifles, revolvers, shotguns, rocket launchers, grenades, crossbows, landmines, C4s, futuristic laser weapons, and of course, the iconic crowbar, ensuring that you never get bored.
Now onto the level design, the level design is very enjoyable, there are parts where you are navigating the facility while avoiding fallen debris, jumping across platforms to avoid falling into toxic waste, destroying military helicopters and tanks in the desert, swimming through water and turning valves, arranging crates together to walk on in order to traverse to a higher area otherwise out of reach, crawling through vents, jumping across elevator shafts, and even jumping and floating around on the colourful alien planet Xen. However I found myself getting stuck a fair amount of times and having to look up a youtube video to find out where to go.
There is nothing more satisfying than killing the final boss and then being congratulated by G-man, a recurring character that wears a suit and holds a briefcase and possesses some sort of unhumanly power. You can see G-man in out of reach areas in the game, however you never interact with him until the end of the game.
The only reason I can see some people hesitating to buy this game is because of the graphics, but I guarantee you, after the first 10-20 minutes of the game, you'll get over it.
Overall, I highly recommend this game to everyone!

TL;DR AT BOTTOM
Very useful, very fun software. Intuitive and a lot of options available for brush customization (and you can download sets from the PGN site or Deviantart or whatever for free, also). Nifty "event" function useful for recording your own drawings if you are interested in creating speedpaints, and being able to load professional-level illustrations right into the OC interface and watch them step-by-step is invaluable to learning from example. Much more intimate than a YouTube video because you can explore every detail of what they're using (type of brush, sensitivity, colour hues, etc). This is an important advantage over Paint Tool SAI and ClipStudio Paint especially if you're interested/motivated in self-teaching.
Also, I am quite fond of how having OpenCanvas being on Steam means it tracks my hours. Personally I enjoy knowing precisely how much time I've spent developing my digital art skills. My friends, who draw also, can also see when I've decided to start drawing something, which creates a nice atmosphere for someone like me. I like how my Steam profile is no longer limited to just gaming but my more expressive hobby is included in as well.
Finally, I have only good things to say about the folks at PGN. I purchased openCanvas 5.5 on Steam well before 6 was released, and I was pleasantly surprised when they told me I could upgrade to 6 at no charge upon its release. OC's developers strike me as refreshingly generous, though for all I know it could have been Valve's decision. In an age where Photoshop (while powerful) is forcing everyone to pay a monthly fee instead of simply buying their software once and for all, OC is cheap and hassle-free alternative. If you're a relative beginner to digital artwork as I was (and probably still am), you don't need all that extra horsepower offered by more costly programs anyway.
tl;dr it's cheap, the unique event function is great for self-teaching, Steam tracks your drawing hours just like any game and the developers seem to be really great folks. I strongly recommend this software if you appreciate these sorts of things.

Gorgeous, hand-rendered art utilizing creative, luscious settings and vibrant colors to set the mood. Fun and unique gameplay coupled with a beautiful and memorable soundtrack. There is a lot to love about this visually arresting game. As fantastic as Bastion is, there were a few things I had problems with in terms of storytelling.
They touched on some sensitive subjects that could have worked well with the story but fell a little short. Basic gist (spoilers abound): Group #1 is part of a community that historically committed atrocities upon a rival community, Group #2. Group #1's resolution to make peace with Group #2 and right wrongs was to...kill a bunch of people from Group #2 and cause more destruction to their home. The narrative was written in a way that everything that happened to Group #2 was self-inflicted, despite it being the player character's fault. That part could have been removed and the story wouldn't have suffered.
The mechanics, art direction, and soundtrack is what makes this game great. The story itself is told over and over again in movies and shows time and time again; a group seeks power by destroying and the oppressed is (rightfully) angry and seeks to avenge their own. No justice is served for the oppressed group and, by the end, it really feels like the game was saying "it was their own undoing" which is morally wrong. It had a lot of potential to tell a deeper story, possibly one of redemption, but they dropped the ball on that.

The 12 Labours of Hercules is part 1/4 of a newly on Steam introduced series of casual time-management flashgames. It has cute and colorful 2.5D graphics and a lovely entertaining soundtrack (one song really sounds like Greek). Placed in the ancient Greek mythology you accomplish many tasks in 40 challenging levels and fight four different bosses. You will also buildup four ancient marvels during the level proccess.

So what is this time-management about?
Basically you start with a static map with blocked pathways and tasks. You give orders to running servants which do several jobs like repair/unblock roads, collect the 3 types of resources (food, wood, gold) and unlock bridges or caves. For each servant one job + 3 additional jobs (shown as flags) you declare their priority list in which order they should complete them. That can become critical in higher levels because everything happens under the pressure of time shown as a shrinking bar on the left side. Lateron you will get the ability to use powerups from another slowly raising bar on the right side. You also have mythology heros like Hercules, Medusa or Pegasus that can remove bolders or fight minotaurs, harpies anfd ghosts for spending food or gold. In the end the choice of the right pathway decides if you win a map with 3 stars or loose. I wouldn't say it's real strategy - just find the hidden pattern once.
Finally I would consider the game is ideal for kids. It's not only completely violentless but challenging and funny. AFAIK it's already published on PurpleHills which means it's somekind of quality assured. Ok the greek mythology is such worthy as "Pirates of the Caribbean" would be a scientific docu about pirates.

In one sentence, I would say that the early access version shows a real committment to being the spiritual successor to MOO/MOO2 that we've all been waiting for. I hope that in a few of the areas that the original MOO/MOO2 didn't do very well that the new development team can innovate enough to bring the game into what we should expect out of a 2016 release.
I can't comment too much on things that still appear to be unfinished - for example, numerous reviews have been pretty critical of the current ship battle experience and I would agree that it is missing a lot of features, but based on its current state compared to how other elements are fleshed out I would say that it will probably get better before the developers are done.
What I would say is that there are a few aspects of the original game that should be more significantly revisited in this version of the game. Two examples are the way that technology influences battle outcomes and how the tech tree implements the restrictive either/or choices from MOO2.
If you played MOO2 you know that a) a more technologically advanced ship pretty much always beats a lesser one and b) a bigger ship is pretty much always better than a smaller one. Because the current combat system is so close to the old one, that's still true, but that's really not the best way to balance gameplay in my opinion. The developers should probably try to evolve the game a bit more so that new tech isn't the automatic win that it is in the old game.
On the tech side, it's improved from the MOO2 system where you were generally given a choice between two or three useful technologies that didn't really make sense to be mutually exclusive; there's only a few times where you have to pick between two different options. However, the ones that are there don't make a lot of sense; for example, you can have either fusion bombs or fusion beams, but never both. It seems like it would make more sense to provide a more sensible system if they want to prevent full access to the entire tech tree. Maybe an affinity system that lets you do certain things better than others in the combat realm - for example, maybe some races can build better shields where others can build bigger ships.
The final comment I will make is that it costs a pretty hefty price and that there are a few things that they need to do to really make it worth that - the textures are currently pretty low resolution in a lot of cases and the art assets are limited in ship building.
Even with the current flaws, I'd still give the game a thumbs up, and if you were waiting for a MOO/MOO2 remake, this is definitely it in my opinion.

Telltale Walking Dead is really Season 1 and by now is well known on many platforms. It is classic Telltale. You play Lee Everett rescues young Clementine whose parents had traveled to Savannah prior to the apocalypse and basically join others in surviving the walking dead where your choices influence the end results of the game. Telltale games are not for everyone, but try one and go from there
Pros
A: It's walking dead seems very familiar to the actual show and its storylines.
B: This has dark wonderful choice driven gameplay.
C: Big plus is all the episodes are done so your not waiting months for a new one.
D: If you love Walking Dead, Zombies, Jerks and its characters this one is for you.
E: Good solid voice acting, nicely animated and straight story telling, pure and simple.
F: PSP PC controller friendly
Cons
A: Your choices may not make much of a difference and I found the game mechanics clunky.
B: Very engaging despite the fact your not really risking bad moves in the game.
C: Follow the game rating, some subject matter not suitable for children. This is walking dead people.
D: Could be a con like most films once you see it once, you may need time to go over it again.
OVERALL: Like all telltale adventures pretty straight forward storytelling with manuevers that can repeated if failed, so no real way to do so. Take a look at gameplay in Workshop. Empty Horizons has touched my soul.
Maybe because it's exactly what I'm into, and I knew that before I bought it. I read the great reviews, was attracted to the description and beautiful artwork, yet I still wasn't expecting to be so captivated. This is now, hands down, my new favorite read.
- The artwork is stunning, especially the female characters--I just couldn't stop staring in awe. The CGs and backgrounds are gorgeous; granted, the interior backgrounds aren't as appealing as the outdoor backgrounds but it hardly matters. There also isn't an extensive variety of backgrounds (or other artwork for that matter), but the story carries itself enough that it still manages to mesh together masterfully with what few assets are presented.
- The music is beautiful. I don't really know what else to say about that, ya get the feels and atmosphere from it and it makes you feel warm and fuzzy inside.
- And last but defintely not least, the writing is spot on. I'm a writer myself and I'm really impressed and inspired. This modern romance story is up to par with the classics, in my opinion. I love stories that focus heavily on dialogue, interactions, and relationship development and that's exactly what this is. And stories like that can be hard to keep people amused but I was enticed by every line. Watching their relationship unfold in a very natural and human way was beautiful and emotional. The characters and the backstory were very well fleshed out. Even those who didn't have much screentime, if any at all, I feel like I knew them well, especially Miri's feelings about them. I'm impressed by that since it's just a few hours of reading give or take.
Definitely worth it. 10/10.

This game an really the whole series have come to dominate my gaming time over the past couple years. It certainly isn't for everyone and the interface can be a bit of a barrier but underneath the hood is a deeply complex and dynamic simulation with no exploits or easy ways to win.
You can build solid teams with whatever offensive and defensive focus you want. If you want to be a coordinator on either side of the ball then there is play design and personell packages to allow for extreme specialization i.e. utilizing screen and YAC based receivers along with deep ball specialists, all this means that it isn't just about getting the best players. However if you just want to GM then the AI does a great job of creating gameplans based on your roster and your opponent. Oh, did I mention the draft. Based upon 6 combine scores and the ratings bars there is still a great level of busts and surprises in the other direction. Height, weight and age also play a big role. And all of this is just the single player experience.
The real gem of this series are the MP leagues and support. I would gladly pay a subscription fee for each MP league but you don't even have to. If you are a simulation nerd buy the dang game, if you are a true football fan who is sick of Madden exploits then buy the dang game. Take your lumps with the interface and get addicted to SP, after a while get yourself in a MP league (or 4) and you will find that there are no sims (sports or otherwise) that even come close to the challenges presented by FOF.
One quick note, the game is published with a help file that is necessary reading and studying material for anyone serious. Along with that there is a great community at
that will help you get up to speed and fill in the intentional gray areas within the help file. As I said, this isn't for everyone but for the right type of customer there is no better gaming experience period.

Personally I give this game an 8/10 in terms of how close it comes to what the game sets out to achieve and what I believe most players are expecting. I started playing FoF 7 a few years ago and I've been hooked ever since. If there's something I really have to stress to anyone on the fence about buying this game who has never played Front office Football before it's that this game isn't for everyone. This game is for people who are looking for the most in depth football text sim, this game has a steep learning curve, and requires a solid time investment to be successful. For those who already own FOF7 I don't feel like there was enough added to the game to justify buying FOF8 outside of the fact that most MP leagues have moved on to FOF8
Some features of the game
-Full Multiplayer leagues. In my opinion this is the #1 reason to buy the game. The SP mode can be fun but in any game like this when you learn enough it becomes a little too easy to beat the AI with consistent success. There are several active MP leagues in FOF8 who are regularly changing ownership and accept players of any skill level. Competing against a full league of other owners is a worthy challenge and makes all stages of the game much more interesting.
Offense:
-Full control of depth chart by formation
-Full control of offensive playbook. You can either generate plays tied to your Offensive Coordinator's philosophy, or you can create all your plays yourself. This allows you to create your own route concepts in the passing game. Playbooks can hold up to 200 plays and you can save playbooks if you want to use them season to season
-Full control of your weekly offensive gameplan. The amount of plays you can use depends on your OC again and allows you to set which plays you want to be called in which situation. Game planning can be tough but gives the player control over your offensive style.
Defense
-A wealth of defensive styles available
-Weekly game plans allow you to play your defense to your team's strengths
-Gives the player control over how often your defense blitzes, plays man / zone, or bump and run coverage. Also has formations that bring the safety into the box for a stronger run defense.
Roster Management / Drafting
-A fairly complex system where player ratings aren't everything and much like the NFL there are underrated players who find in game success and high rated players who under perform.
-Player ratings that are never perfect. The game uses your coaches' scouting ability to determine the ratings you see, a player's true rating can differ fairly significantly from the ratings you see. The more years a player has been in the league the closer your scouted ratings will be to a players true rating.
-A draft system that is truly more of an art than a science. You're not going to find your 6th round Tom Brady but for those who are willing to put the time in you can start to identify solid role players deep into the draft.
-A contract negotiation system that is tied to player production as well as skill. Unproven players or players who have under performed recently will sign for a discount. Low-average rated players who have impressive seasons statistically will demand more money.
-Player hold outs and satisfaction. Some players who feel underpaid will hold out of the preseason for a better contract. Other players may become unhappy due to lack of starting time or because they have a conflict with another player. Unhappy players may refuse to sign with a team altogether.
Cons/Criticisms
-The UI. Personally I find it manageable / tolerable but I have seen many people complain about the UI over my time on the FOFC forums and feel it should be mentioned that this is something some people really don't care for.
-Lack of control in more subtle ways. There's no such thing as a "zone run" scheme, no such thing as bringing a 6th OL in as a TE, and no way to put your TE in the slot unless you play him as a slot WR in a certain formation. Also you cannot choose which player will be blitzing from a defensive formation altough you can influence it to more often be your best pass rusher.
-The game seems to favor the short passing game / screen game over throwing the ball 10-15 yards down the field. (opinion)
-Running backs can get way more touches in a season than would be realistic if they have high enough endurance.

I have played FOF7 and FOF8.
FOF8 makes a number of improvements to the game. You can now choose your plays directly focusing on a single impact player if you wish. There is some of these features for the defense, but it is not nearly as dynamic as the offense.
A criticism is the manner in which you choose your plays. You give a number and it picks plays for you. However, if you opt to not use it, forget going back to it. The nes time you pick that number it will be a different set of plays. The system makes it difficult to choose from existing plays. If you do want to focus on certain players, then you need to build the play from scratch. This is enormously time consuming.
On the defensive side of the ball, you have less choices. Depending on the formation, you have certain defensive defenses. However, these choices are limited. It is difficult to choose a specific blitzer in a given defensive set. It isn't perfect, but I can how people would want more choices to put guys they have in better positions to be successful. You are more or less force to play conventinal defenses.
When it comes to chosing your coaches, it is a real crap shoot. In the real world, you compete to hire coaches. The game it is more like a draft. In multiplayer it is even worse uness you have "live draft." You can literally spin your wheels trying to get a good coach. In multiplayer, the coaches are not part of any cap on salary so any team can have a descent coach nearly indefinitely.
The most comnfusing aspect of the game is the bars. In a QB on team with rating in the mid to upper 70s and on another team I have a QB with mostly high 30s. Their performances are on par despite having similar talent around them. The game is screwy here. Injries are incredibly high. In one season I lost nearly my entire DL and I still had third of my season to go. In fact i managed three teams and two of them 10 plus injuries on t eht eam in which more three players more or less out for the year. Now, teams do have this happened, but I managed three teams for about 4 seasons each and I had these sort of numbers for nearly every season. It was the "normal."
The coaches make weird decisions in the game. In two different games, I had the ball inside the 5 yard line with about 45- to min left in both games. Instead of killing the clock and taking a coule of shots, I kick a FG in both cases. That is just dumb. The game will make these weird decisoons all the time. It also seems to be stuck in a narrative. I had a few seasons when I literally lost every game in nearly similar circumstances. I mean I was laughing at the insanity; I literally predicted what was going to happen nearly everytime. One significant problem I noticed is one of my teams have a run blocking OL and a good running back and a great FB. I rushed for 5, 11, 6, 4, 7, 5, 4 . The next play I do a play action. Sack??? It happened all season long. In some cases, I would get a FG, but mostly, I didn't. I figured out that players do not get affected pshychologically by being run on. So, clearly I liked this game quite a bit, considering I have 97 hours logged on Steam. But I don't think I can wholeheartedly reccommend it. I have never played Fallout 1 or 2, but I have played a lot of 3 and New Vegas, and really enjoyed them both. Fallout 4, on the other hand, does a few significant things differently, in a way that made it difficult for me to enjoy the game without a ton of modding.
Criticism #1: The voice-acted player character. The acting itself is not bad by any means, but for me, it gets in the way of the roleplaying aspect of the game. When the player character is silent, I can mentally fill in the blanks myself and more easily put myself in their shoes, immerse myself in the world. When the protagonist has a pre-recorded set of voice lines, it feels less like I'm going on an adventure myself and more like I'm arbitrarily choosing a path for someone else's story.
Criticism #2: The dialogue system. Bethesda tried to streamline the dialogue option-choosing process by breaking down each of your four choices into a word or two that vaguely describes the intent of the line ("sarcastic," "yes," "threaten," etc.) rather than outright telling you what your character will say. I understand the motive behind this design choice but ultimately I thought it hurt the experience. For one thing, there are now only ever four choices available at a time - one for each face button - whereas before, they could list as many as they wanted, giving the player more freedom. Additionally, and more importantly, the one or two words the game gives you very frequently doesn't accurately convey the impact of the full line, and so you will often end up making choices semi-blind or will get an unfavorable outcome from a conversation because you misunderstood what the dialogue option meant.
Both of the above criticisms can largely be remedied by installing a few mods, but another fundamental problem I had with Fallout 4 can't really be fixed - the story. It's not bad, but it's just not as compelling as I found 3 and New Vegas to be. And because the whole narrative is framed as a revenge/resuce story, it very quickly feels out of place when you're doing anything but the main quest, even more so than past Bethesda games.
Those are my main criticisms. Here are some other pros and cons:
+By far the most beautiful and visually detailed Fallout game
+Great soundtrack and sound design
+Vastly improved combat
+Interesting, large world to explore - Boston is a great setting
-Not as many interesting or compelling side characters and quests as previous games
-Animations are still very stiff and janky across the board, especially when compared to other contemporary AAA open-world games like The Witcher 3 or Breath of the Wild
-Main quest endings feel oddly anticlimactic and underwhelming
Basically, if you loved Fallout 3 and/or New Vegas and are itching for more Fallout to play, then by all means, go for it. But if you've never played a Fallout game before, I'd suggest you go with 3 or NV.

I have been playing this game for a few years now, though all of that time was on browser and not steam.
I absolutely love this game, and i will willingly say im addicted to it, no matter how badly i play or how many times i die.
Looking on steam's reviews i see lots of Not Recommendeds just because of Kabam making it "Pay to Win"...
Let me give you my two cents on the game as-is.
First, the game itself.
This is an 8-Bit MMO, where you run around killing monsters (Either by staves, arrows, or....Throwing swords?) to build up your character of choice, Beat up dungeon bad guys and hang out with people online.
It is also a BULLET HELL Game, with a PERMANENT DEATH feature. If you die, you DIE. Restart your whole character. The only things you dont lose when you die are your Pet (Sent back to your pet yard, ill explain in a bit), your Fame you've earned, and Realm gold youve bought.
One of the major goals in this game is (Or was, really) to obtain the Legendary White star. This meant that you had to earn enough fame to get 5 stars on each class.
Fame is earned by, well...Killing stuff. A whole lot. The main point of having it now though, is for pet feeding (Ill get to it shortly! Hold on!), along with just collecting it to earn that star.
A second? Beat up oryx for what he's put you through. That one happens regularly and is more of a dungeon run than a goal, per se.
Finally, Maxing out your character's stats (Done by Potion drinking, potions of various types being earned from different dungeons) and grabbing the best loot possible are a third goal.
There are 13 classes, each having a different stat total and a different secondary weapon skill to use and abuse.
When you start on steam, though, youll only have access to 5 of the 13, with the other 8 accessed by either earning them (Get 1 or 2 other classes to Level 20, nothing hard) or by buying them (NOT recommended, the classes will cost you 5-10 bucks each)
Youll start off at Level 1, with a tutorial to guide you through the basics. WASD for moving, Mouse and click for shooting, How to grab loot, etc.. Everything else is explained in your Options (O key).
From there, youre dumped into one of the various "Realms" where you fight against Oryx's minions. You'll run around, killing "Quest monsters" for exp (They...really are just that. Go around and kill them, no point other than EXP and loot)
and upgrading as you go. Different bosses will teach you different attack patterns to learn in this game. Deathmages will fire where you will be (Level ~6 quest boss, and they HURT without defense), Ents will fire where you are (Lvl 10+ Quest mobs, which need to die along with other bosses to "Close the realm" and fight oryx), and so on. From your very first character, itll take about a half an hour to get to Level 20.
But wait, theres more! MUCH more! Now that youre level 20 you get to "Max your character's Stats" By means of stat potions! There are 8 potions to collect and drink, and the bonuses (Up to max) are permanent until your character dies.  There are many ways to collect them, but most revolve around dungeon running when the dungeon presents itself.
Most people will sit around and farm in the "Godlands" (A place where long ranges thrive and sword classes need defense to last long in) on the basic map. You'll usually see where it is, as at any time or occasion theres a mob of people  at lvl 20 there farming. Takes awhile, though.
Your other choice will be dungeon running, which works in an interesting way. Dungeons arent "Accessed" immediately unless you buy the key for gold. No, you have to kill a certain enemy until it drops. Sounds hard? Nah, most dungeons that have basic stat potions drop fairly common.
Another thing to note about dungeons: If you enter a dungeon solo, you are guaranteed whatever potion the boss drops for you (With a few exceptions)
If you are with others, only ONE person will have a guaranteed potion drop. Everyone else will have a CHANCE to get the potion (A fairly decent chance, to be honest)
Once you have a fair bit of experience in the game, itll be time to work on a few other things. For one, (And this is a BIG ONE now that it's in game) you need a PET. Well, WANT a pet.
When pets were introduced, they initially did nothing other than cosmetics. Kabam, however, decided to change that, so they give crazy boosts when you pour the time and items into them.
Your items you pick up have a "Feed" value, which means thats how many points your pet will get when you feed it to them.
Feeding costs either FAME or GOLD. You do not have to be good to farm a pet to help you.
When you work on a pet, my advice is that you should find one with Heal and MP heal for the 1st 2 skills your pet has (The skills are randomized with each egg you open).
When you get a pet, most likely (Unless you buy an uncommon or higher egg through gold (I Do NOT recommend this until you have a pet you want to work on)) it will be a Common Grade. Youll need fame to upgrade your yard and upgrade your pet to a higher Grade. The boosts wont be too noticeable at first, but when the pet reaches uncommon and higher, youll see it...
DISCLAIMER: Despite what others think, a Divine grade pet will NOT save you if youre in a horrible position.
Another thing to learn is the Market system, which is fairly simple. Players have established prices for many items in game, with a common currency item being Defense potions; Defense pots being chosen mainly for their high need to survive higher grade dungeons. Most items you would want to start rebuilding your character (Or have high power in your attacks and such) are about 1-2 defense potions each. Many later game items you can get have skyrocketed prices for slight power gains, so stick with items on Tier 10 (Ill explain items next) or so until you have potions to spare.
But how could i forget...I need to explain items! Armors (Robes, leathers and metal armors) are from Tier 1 to Tier 13, Weapons (6 different types) are from 1 - 12, and Everything else for the most part is from T1-T6 or T1-T5 (Majorly being rings and secondaries for each class). The beginning items suck (Obviously) while the end game items, while being very powerful, jump in power from T7+, but tend to gain marginal increases after T10+.
Finally, You may wish to join a Guild. Do i need to explain that one? It works about the same as any other game,
While i do love this game for its positive things, i hate it for a few bad things. For one, Whenever a realm shuts down, something happens called "Oryx lag". This means for 3 seconds ish, youll "Rubber band" (Enemies and players will fly off, only to come back in a slightly different spot when the lag is done. This lag type also happens when YOU or REALM lags, so be careful if it happens. It can END you.) and need to watch yourself. Some enemies can instantly murder you if youre not careful and lagging.
Another is the community, to a certain extent. While i will NEVER say it's as bad as, say, Maplestory's community (And Waaaaaaaay far better than Transformice's community), It does have a few bad eggs in there. Youll find good people easily though.
Finally? Kabam. This is the main hate people give this game. Kabam made this game...More pay for ease and success in many ways. You can still earn your way though; there is no such thing as a player in this game having a better character than you just because they bought Realm gold. Do i recommend this? Yes. This game is fun and tends to be satisfying when all of your work pays off.
It's not for people who want instant gratification, or hate when most to all progress is lost on death, but if you get past that and slight grinding this game is a blast. It's worth a look, definitely.

Just finished playing through a full game. Many lesser issues which I will not spend time on in this post. Two major issues hurt the game however. Number 1 is the star lanes which were a terrible idea in MOO 3 and should never have been copied to this new itteration. MOO 1 and 2 were about free travel and exploration in space. The forced star lanes here dumb down the overall strategy and promote huge fleets building up at choke points. Developers claim star lanes are the more popular choice (doubt it), but at least make an option for no star lanes in game set up. The second major fault is tactical comabat (the complete lack of it). Its supposed to be a hybrid of RTS (real time strategy) but is more like RTW (real time witness). You can pause the action at any time in battle to "take control" but besides steering different groups of ships and changing their formation, there is nothing to do. You can chose tactical mode and watch the battle happen with nice graphics, or you can skip that and just get the results with a simulate option. In "tactical" you have no control over individual ships (groupings only), no control over weapons fire, and cannot tell damaged ships to pull back or retreat from the battle. There is nothing meaningful to do. The developers said turn based combat was too slow so they dropped it for real time, but at least turn based combat was meaningful and really impacted game play. These real time battles seem decided almost entirely by math rather than tactics and are neither engaging or memorable.
All told the game does capture much of the same atmosphere of MOO 1 and 2 and it has development potential. Wait and see how they address the problems before buying though. They haven't earned our money yet.

I don't know why they call this the 12 labours of Hercules, as he is napping in a hammock most of the time. Your servants are the real heroes in this game. Extremely simple concept with only one mouse button required.
The game is split into 4 chapters, as Hercules chases the man who kidnapped his wife. You have a global map where each level is displayed. The game is linear--you can only go one way to get to the end. You must complete each mission in order.
Once you select the mission, you begin with typically one servant and a napping Hercules. You must complete the objectives, such as collect a feather, and collect 80 gold. The mechanics are simple--issue a servant to complete a task, such as chop a tree down and bring back the lumber. The servant will do it provided you have enough of the resources required.
This is why it's a game and not a bore:
. You decide what your laborers do. The idea is to plot out a strategy in which all your workers will be performing operating in harmony. For example, sometimes it will cost food to chop a tree to get lumber. You predict this and already have another worker getting the food to make up for the loss. There is a time limit, and the faster you complete the mission, the better your score. The missions can be completed any way you choose, even if you are terrible at resource management, you will find a way to complete the mission.
The game has two difficulties, casual--which I have just completed, and expert (which I will definitely be doing). For $0.29 on sale, you get trading cards worth approximately the same amount. You likely won't profit by playing this game, but if you sell the cards, you may just get it for free!

The most memorable one is the mission to hunt down fourteen small ostriches to pedal the turbines to make a huge hot air balloon float of into the air, so a species of hairy-looking creatures can escape to the skies.
All in all though, it’s a beautiful game visually and soundwise which I would rate very highly indeed.

Wow this game. It's essentially TF2 competative or DOTA in space, you're split into 5 man teams and have to capture the enemies base.
I see a lot of reviews knocking it for being P2W, but it's not. I haven't spent a dime and wreck ships well. You can pay money to support the devs and get ships and premium skins, or you can play for days to get one or two ships and weeks to get a skin. Take your pick. The game gives you premium currency twice a week for log on bonuses and you can get rare loot from mission drops.
Missions are the real point of the game. They get you crew members, crew experience, credit boosters, and sometimes rare 'epic' loot like ship skins or premium currency. I've played for 43 hours at the time of this review and have gotten 3 epic drops. I can now defend a point with +10% defence, +3% more attack, and some new colors. Winning a round gets you twice as many credits, but credit boosters get you even more.
There's nothing wrong with the starter ship (Pioneer). It's an attack ship that relies on mobility and excels at taking down stealth ships. It is not a god ship that can wreck the entire team. There is no such single ship.
Speaking of which, this is a team game. You're only as good as your weakest team member and even the best pilots can fail if they don't work with their team. One of the main problems with this game, like most MMO's, are it's toxic community. If you aren't politely explaining to your teammates what they're doing wrong and helping them to get better then they aren't the problem, you are. I've turned noobs into pilots and in doing so have gathered a fine crew.
10/10, would destroy a destroyer in a pioneer again.

I don't think Tower Unite can really be summarized or reviewed in the way you generally review a game. I say this because in a way this game isn't really a game, as it's more of a social hub; like social media. As cringey as it may sound coming from a furry on the internet, Tower Unite is really a great game for those who lack good social skills out in the real world.
Due to the in-depth nature of some categories, the review will be structured to show the most basic information first, then going more in-depth on the same topic. The format will look like this:
Example:
There's not just one kind of gameplay in Tower Unite, seeing as there are many activites to do. For an overally summary, though, Tower Unite's gameplay is what you'd expect from a social hub game; you can go around doing multiple activities with your friends, which adds a lot of variety to the gameplay.
Most of what you do in Tower Unite will take place in the Plaza. Everything from buying furniture to gambling your money, it'll take place here. Most of your social things like conversation, meetups, etc. will take place here. The Plaza also contains the highest building, which is the Tower Condos building where everyone lives.
In The Tower, hence the name "Tower Unite", players can go to the front desk and open their Condo. You can select to go in alone, allow friends to join, or allow any amount of random players in. Players can access eachother's public condos either by going to the Tower and entering through one of many doors, or on the main menu from a server list.
You can go to a total of 8 stores in the Plaza.
This includes: Sweet Suite Furnishings for most furnishing needs, Central Circuit for things like working TVs and other devices, Songbirds which sells functional instruments and decorations, Seasons which has everything you need for a garden, Rob's Imports for miscellaneous items, The Toystop for playful items, Celebrations for celebratory goodies, and Fresh for food. More shops are in development.
In Sweet Suite Furnishings you can buy things like sofas, tables, and beds. Most of your shopping will be done here if you like decorating your home.
If you wanna watch TV at your place you're gonna wanna visit this store. You can buy TVs, monitors, potato computers and more.
Songbirds sells high-end instruments that actually function. You can find sheet music for the instruments online, mainly for the Grand Piano.
Seasons is the newest store and contains some of the oldest stuff ever; plants. Ranging from tiny flowers to giant trees, this bird has it. (A bird owns the place, it's amazing.)
Rob's Imports sells some pretty random furniture pieces and will soon contain community-made Steam Workshop items in it. It's also where you buy the jetpack to fly around.
The Toyshop has everything your childish heart would desire. This palce even has a giant wooden T-Rex skeleton you can buy for 10,000 Units.
Celebrations has everything you need for a party. The most commonly bought items are fireworks that people usually light off in the Plaza.
Fresh is currently a pretty empty place, but once Pixeltail adds in cooking, you'll be able to purchase ingredients from there to use to make your own food at home.
The Plaza has it's own little games you can play on the fly, without needing to set up a lobby.
This includes: The Casino for gambling, Laser Tag which is an FPS, the Bowling Alley for bowling, Trivia to test your brain, and Typing Derby where you type words to race others.
The Casino is another realm of activities in itself. There are three different slot machines you can play on, Texas Hold'Em Poker, Double Or Nothing which is a chance game, Video Blackjack, and Video Poker. With your money you can play Spin To Win for 500 Units at a chance for a special item.
Laser Tag is a pretty standard shooter mode set inside a laser tag arena, which is beautifully designed with neon and futuristic architecture. Your goal is to eliminate all the other teams' players and stay alive. Each player gets 3 lives.
The Bowling Alley is just what it says it is. It contains 8 lanes which can hold 4 players each. It's fun but simple with great controls.
Trivia is a pretty basic game with user-submitted questions from the community. You and 5 other players have 4 buttons to choose from that you use to select 1 of 4 answers to the question on the screen. The better you do, the more Units you make.
Typing Derby holds up to 8 players who have 90 seconds to type the words given on the screen. They begin easy and get harder as you go further. First player to wins gets the most Units. The longer you go without messing up earns you bonuses at the end.
There are some smaller and more obscure things to do in Tower Unite, mainly the Theater and the Poseidon ride. Future plans include things like fishing which is currently being made.
The Tower Theatre as it's called lets you select media from Youtube, Soundcloud, and Twitch to watch with other players in real time. The same thing can be done in a condo with a media-enabled device from Circuit Central.
Poseidon is a nice roller coaster that the developers added in that can actually be kinda fun with friends. Definitely try it at least once.
The Game Hub is much like the Tower, as in it's just another way to get somewhere. Here a player can go to select from one of the Gameworlds and anyone in the same server will be notified someone is starting a match for it and give them the option to instantly join from wherever they are. The Game Hub contains all of the Gameworlds that are on the main menu.

Telltale Walking Dead is really Season 1 and by now is well known on many platforms. It is classic Telltale. You play Lee Everett rescues young Clementine whose parents had traveled to Savannah prior to the apocalypse and basically join others in surviving the walking dead where your choices influence the end results of the game. A simple point click watch what happens game. If you love Walking dead a must. If you don't but like other Telltale games, not a bad game to add. Telltale games are not for everyone, but try one and go from there
Pros
A: It's walking dead seems very familiar to the actual show and its storylines.
B: This has dark wonderful choice driven gameplay.
C: Big plus is all the episodes are done so your not waiting months for a new one.
D: If you love Walking Dead, Zombies, Jerks and its characters this one is for you.
E: Good solid voice acting, nicely animated and straight story telling, pure and simple.
F: PSP PC controller friendly
Cons
A: Your choices may not make much of a difference and I found the game mechanics clunky.
B: Very engaging despite the fact your not really risking bad moves in the game.
C: Follow the game rating, some subject matter not suitable for children. This is walking dead people.
D: Could be a con like most films once you see it once, you may need time to go over it again.
OVERALL: Like all telltale adventures pretty straight forward storytelling with manuevers that can repeated if failed, so no real way to do so. Take a look at gameplay in Workshop. See the video gameplay to see if you like it. If Adventures are your thing. This is a must have and one of Telltales best. A solid game. I would wait till it is on sale at 50/75% off. I got about 6 Telltale titles that way, and not a bad game to have in your library. My Score 3.8 out of 5.0

I'm going to start this review off by going as far as to claim that I enjoyed this title even more than I have Key's critically acclaimed titles (CLANNAD and Planetarian). I'm not claiming this is the best story I've ever read or the greatest VN of all time, but for me it is up there.
Empty Horizons is a rather short Visual Novel in the sense that you might finish it within a few hours (it took me a little bit over two to finish the first route, but I am a rather quick reader). I'd say the term kinetic novel is more fitting than visual novel, honestly, as there are two choices that you get access to after completing the game once. What I have stated may be a bit of a deterrent to those that want a choice laden or lengthy game, so I counter by saying that the game has a story that I found to be masterfully crafted and despite reading everything in nearly four hours - I skipped repeat text – I've spent far longer with the story because my brain keeps cycling through it three days later; the story has had a lasting effect on me and is one that I will likely remember for the rest of my (hopefully) long life.
In addition to the story, the VN comes with the following extras: a CG Gallery, Bonus Art, a Music Box, and Notes from the author (notes that I found really insightful and enjoyable). On the subject of what the game contains, it does not contain voice acting, but I regard that as a plus because it would have cut over the game's excellent soundtrack. I wasn't a fan of the artwork in the beginning, but it quickly grew on me, so if you aren't wild about the look, maybe it'll grow on you over time?
I want to leave a longer review, but I am unsure how to do so without spoiling anything and the author's description of the game says all that can really be said on it without spoiling. As an individual that loves to read nearly everything I can get my hands on, I cannot recommend Empty Horizons enough.
If you are still unsure then maybe wait until the Ebi-Hime Bundle or Empty Horizons goes on sale and pick this game up either alone or with some of Ebi-Hime's other Visual Novels.

openCanvas attempts to imitate the good parts of programs such as Photoshop and SAI but ultimately fails, providing a lackluster software with no shining traits of its own. The basics are well enough - drawing and sketching are stabilized, and if you do purchase this project you can work with it just fine. Unfortunately, the projects' bugs and subpar tools mean that it should not be your first choice of drawing software.
I mainly use this program offline, so my use of it is more in the 25+ hours range rather than the 3 shown on steam.
Pros:
-Good for sleek, strong lines and flat coloring; doing lineart is a pleasure.
-Provides several tools from Photoshop: image warping, transformations, text, layer effects, etc.
-Not especially heavy on the system.
-Has handy preset guides for various types of lines and perspective.
-Lets you adjust pen pressure.
Cons:
-Terrible selection/customization of brushes - some of the basic ones lag too much to use.
-In detail: The preset brushes have very little variety, and there are only the following options to customize: opacity, size, spacing, hardness, pressure. So, you can make a super sharp thin pen! Or a blurry soft pen! Or a blurry thin set of dots! You can add your own pen nibs (shapes/textures) for better customization, but when you lack options such as rotation and randomness settings, how much you can do with it becomes limited.
-Brushes and colors do not blend; instead, works via opacity like Photoshop painting, so it's difficult to get a good "painted" look.
-MANY minor bugs which add up to an inconvenient and sometimes annoying experience while drawing. Every startup or scroll through the drawing generates a pop up error window; after reopening drawing, there are sometimes visual glitches which thankfully go away after minimizing and reopening the window; the transparency slider gets 'stuck' so you have to reopen the drawing to get it to work again; some shortcuts don't work (for example, I can't get the layer duplicate shortcut to work despite having it properly assigned).
-The non-freeform lining/drawing is clunkily handled - there's no pen tool. Instead, you can make curves by poking two dots at the start and end of the line and 'dragging out' the apex of the curve. You have very little control over the shape of the curve, and can't edit it to fix it (except by manually redrawing, of course). The polygonal or line tools work better.
-Has weak effects - gaussian blur has an upper limit of, vaguely, "10", which is just enough to soften the edges, I guess.
-Airbrush seems to tone down the colors; I usually use it to add some vividness/highlights/blush, but the airbrush makes it look greyer/drabber.
-(Negligible) Can't do pixel art with this, even the smallest size brush/pencil set with 100% opacity makes semi-transparent marks across two squares.
Overall, the software is "okay", and if you're a decent artist you can make good work with it; it's not bad enough to sabotage your work, but not good enough that it provides anything to help you go above and beyond compared to if you used a different software. Its only real distinguishing trait is the ability to record your drawing (which I personally don't use, and can't comment on). If you need something compatible with photoshop and which has transparency, this works fine, but only that. Regardless of whatever style you're working on, there's a better (and possibly cheaper) software out there for you.
Bottom line though: if you like drawing cell-shaded cartoons/anime, this is ok. If you're into painting digitally, don't get this.

This one is a nice blend between Artrage 4 and Manga Studio (Paint Clip), which I also got, I use photoshop CC, and Mischief as well.
And Open Canvas is a great drawing/painting/inking program, you won't be able to do a lot of the editing you could do in Photoshop, but for drawing/painting great pieces, you can't go wrong with Open Canvas, like most programs it will probably take you some time to get used to it's small differences.
On Steam, this is probably the best program in that category. Photoshop is still my go to program, since I'm more familiar with it, but Open Canvas got stylus stabilizer options, which will make inking easier, there are also other brush options I really like in Open Canvas compared to PS CC, but those might vary in use from person to person, in which case like so many other drawing/painting programs, there are many great ones out there, and there really isn't any evil, in trying or using more than one. But you if you are searching for something to directly replace PS CC, I don't think this is it, nor do I believe there is any, for that matter.
This program will however offer a more focused drawing experience, with tools to greatly help you save time, when it comes to just sketching, drawing, inking, and painting.
It also has an event log, like a big history log, which is possibly a great tool, for step by step, seeing and understanding, what exactly the artist did to create, like watching over their shoulders, opens up for faster understanding of advanced methods, if shared.

Colin McRae Rally is not a good game. The controls are very poor, bordering on nigh unplayable at times. The cars bounce more than bobble heads and are ridiculously easy to flip and crash with simple traversing over a simple jump at low speeds. The game offers four cars that have zero difference in handling or acceleration with three of them being locked until progress is made into the championships. There are a number of different championships to play thru and each becomes progressively more difficult.
The game runs fine, looks decent, and could have the potential to be better if a patch to fix the car physics and controls were introduced. For the first few hours, you'll likely tolerate the controls, but after a couple of hours past the point of no longer being refundable, you realize that this was not a good investment. The game does have steam cards and steam achievements so at least those work properly.
Not recommended, not even on a good sale. Save your money for something better.

In a nuttshell this is a fun game.    There are plenty of reviews from folks giving this a thumbs down and I've read through most of them.   Nearly every negative comment is due to the game not being finished yet, I still don't understand the folks who buy an "Early Access" game and expect it to not have some issues with it......c'mon people you are basicaly play testing for them so they can have TONS of input on what to fix before the full launch!
Things the Devs are working on that most have commented about.  The AI is crap, yup it's extremely easy right now and they did that for a reason.  If you make it too difficult, and we all have seen that, then folks will simply throw up their hands because it's frustrating playing against an AI that is basically getting inside information or has built it cheats that allow it to progress faster.  Having a true balanced AI is extremely difficult, but they are working on it.
Combat can be improved upon but many of the comments I've seen are bunk.  You can control your ships to a degree, you can select which targets they shoot at, you can change formations, you can send them anywhere on the map you want (in groups or individual ships).  You cannot choose which weapons to shoot and you cannot target specific things on the enemy ships.  It's very simplistic combat that you can actually effect the outcome of the battle.....I know, I've tested it many times and have watched my fleet lose battels they would normally easily win by me making bold and too aggressive actions.  I've also won fights that I probably would have lost if I had not manipulated my ships properly around the map.
Deplomacy is something that the Devs have said is a work in progress.  Not sure what these people are talking about that the AI players are forcing them to give up tech or they "get mad at you".  Um, yeah, that's kinda the way the world works presently so it's only fitting.   The AI will get upset if you don't share but it doesn't attack you, it doesnt do anything other then pout.   No matter what you do though it really doesnt matter, the AI is so easy to beat you can share all you want and you will still win.  Again, it's something they will ramp up later and then we'll hear all the crying about it being too difficult.
The game feels very old school, is a lot of fun to play, and will get better as they add more races and tweak the AI.   Any game that I can sit down and start playing and by the next time I look at the clock it's 5hrs later is a thumbs up!

Starbound is a special sort of game. It manages to scratch the itch that games like No Man's Sky provided pre-launch while also staying grounded with a sense of identity. While inevitably being compared to Terraria, Starbound is a little different. In terraria, you have a checklist, (i.e. get metal, dig to the underworld, fight the bosses, etc.), whereas in Starbound you have a story accompanying this checklist. However, the checklist is less prominent due to the in-depth RNG creating the planets you explore. You can get any ore at any time if you simply survive to that point. While still an excellent game, Starbound still has its flaws. Crafting is slightly clunky, armor tiers aren't laid out in a concise way, some abilities are questionable in value, and despite the frequent updates, many "legacy" items are quickly outdated by new upgrade systems.

All in all, Starbound is an excellent game with a ton of potential. With the 1.0 update looming, i personally can't wait to see what Chucklefish has in wait for us.
Final Score: 9.3/10

A love story, as one might think. Is it truly..?
If you want to know if it's worth to play it but are to lazy to read everything, jump right down to the last part.
You're a man. A man in a house, destroyed and old. You seem happy in a depressed surrounding. As you come close to anything in this house, the man says nice things about things in it, telling about his life and stories that are held within those things. Everything is special in this house. There's one thing though - you're alone. And you're looking around the little house for someone - Serena. Try to find her. That means, if she is in fact in the house.
There is something wrong with you too. You don't feel sick. Yet from the start you feel that something must be wrong with you. That is the best part of the game - you shouldn't focus on finding out about Serena - you should focus on finding yourself.
Little gameplay spoiler here:
The place is small, there is a door outside but as much as I wanted to go outside - nope, you won't be able to go. Some people might be scared by the though alone to go out to the forest - don't be.
Controls? Mouse only. At least that's the only thing you should be using. To make the mood hit you more. And headphones, or at least make it dark in your room so there's no sunlight.
The man is very interesting and in fact it's really nice every time you make his personality evolve. The only problem I had with that evolving - if you can make a percentage graph based on a persons feelings - first he's 0%, then 100%, then 50%. That goes a bit to fast in my opinion.
Conclusion:
The game is short, hitting less than 50 minutes of play time if you explore every corner and item in your house and listen to every dialog. The atmosphere becomes heavier the more you find out about your past - the progressing of your own mind is something that is really worth to see. Do I recommend it? Yes, I do. That's not a long game and the story and atmosphere is good enough to make those 50 minutes memorable. Even if you're someone who's often afraid of horror games - this one is not one of the games that make you jump all the time. Definitely an experience worth to go through and make acquaintance with.

's good.
It's got some serious design flaws, to be fair: there's a lot of things in this game that you'll need to progress but not know how to get. You're probably going to spend a lot of time on the two wikis for the game (yes, there are two wikis for the game; and neither of them are quite up to date yet), but this is still a beta, so I'm hoping they'll fix that issue and teach you a bit more about how to make certain tools. The system in place now lends itself to being a little fetch-questy.
There's a lot of character customization options, which I approve of, but for some reason, you can craft different color dyes, but you can't actually use them (to my knowledge). Regardless of that, there's still tons of different types of equipment you can wear. It helps that each of the seven races has their own unique armor per armor tier that can be worn by the different races.
I absolutely love the Matter Manipulator, which takes the place of your typical fare of different level pickaxes. You can upgrade it to be able to mine blocks faster, mine liquids, mine in a larger area, and it's automatically got a lot more range than pickaxes, which makes it a far more versatile tool. You can still make pickaxes to mine faster, but I've found that I usually forget I have them, which means they're basically taking up space in my inventory.
I also like the sci fi setting; it's a good change of pace from your typical semi-fantasy setting for these kinds of mining games (I'm looking at you, Minecraft and Terraria), and the setting itself is pretty great. The different races all feel unique and original; like, there's still the stereotypical "Warrior/Savage" race, but who would have thought it would be the flower-people? I wouldn't. I didn't.
Basically, if you're in my position (tired to death of Minecraft, want a long game, want lots of different items/playstyles) buy it. It's like 15 bucks for hours of content. If you're like me and you like making new characters in these kinds of games, it will behoove you to know that all your characters live in the same game-world, which means you can share all the items you get among your characters. Certain parts will only be difficult once because of this (just get a bazillion core fragments and keep them in a chest) if you choose to play that way, which means that you'll be able to get through the game much faster, if that's how you want to play.
In conclusion; much good very buy so enjoy wow

Much like Asphyxia, this visual novel (by the same developer) is a bit depressing. Unfortunately, it's quite short, but still definitely worth the read.
The protagonist is Mireille, an eighteen year old girl whose father has just died. Although she is half-French and half-Italian, she doesn't know a word of French and has never visited France. After living in Italy her whole life, she is now expected to live with her uncle in France, as he's the closest relative. Charged with bringing her to France is a Frenchman, employed by her family, named Lyon. The relationship between Mireille and Lyon is complex and amusing, as it fluctuates frequently between love and hate. The story takes a drastic turn shortly after they cross the border into France.
According to the developer, the working title for this VN was "Spicy Sexism" which makes a lot sense as you read it. While there are lots of sexist comments, it's all satirical, showing how ridiculous such prejudices are.
I would've liked more choices and branching paths, but the story was still enjoyable. The artwork was gorgeous. I do recommend this VN.

Each edition of Front Office Football brings a new element, and the eighth version offers the deepest, most immersive simulation yet while remaining appealing to novice and veteran users.
The biggest addition to FOF8 is the game planning expansion. For the first time in any football sim, users can simulate what it's like to build a game plan just like real NFL coordinators. You can choose packages that fit your personnel as well as build game plans that attack your opponent's weaknesses.
The stats and records of FOF8 add another level of immersion, with the ability to track players' progress throughout their careers. The different game levels and ability to assign duties to your coaches allows you to spend as much or as little time playing through a career. Sometimes I want to just play the role of GM, while other times I want to micromanage everything. You can do it all in FOF8.
The customer service from Solecismic is personal and amazing. So much of the feedback from fans goes into the game and its updates and future editions. Cannot recommend the game enough if you're a football fan and want a real football sim and not a video game.

An amazing game with an original storyline and beautiful soundtrack, Bastion is by far one of the most unique games any one person can play. The concept of an interactive storyline takes on a whole new meaning because of this game and I have yet to witness any other game emulate the power and originality this game exhibits on so many levels. Combining profound concepts with great music, artistic graphics, and a sort of post-apocalyptic scene of its own, Bastion is less of a game and more of a story that you play to hear. For those of you seeking to play the best, most interesting, and original games out there, I cannot recommend Bastion enough. You will not be disappointed.

Highly recommend this game; the developers are active and genuinely care about the future of the game, and while they aren't perfect, they are willing to listen to community feedback. Regarding the game itself, it can be a bit overwhelming to get into at first, so I'd highly recommend joining the official Discord server and asking questions about stuff there. There's always a few veteran players on that are happy to offer tips, and you can find other new players to play with, as well. Definitely a quality game, certainly worth giving a shot to see if it's something you might like!

Another update is that custom races are available, but cannot be saved, still a miss from the developers. And finally, older games cannot be replayed or continued, so there's no backward compatibility between game versions.

After going commercial there are some improvements, however, the perks "huge starting planet" and "heavy gravity" still need to be merged. This is a very stupid thought that these are separate, I cannot think of one reason a race with a huge home world would have a grvity penalty; huge world=high gravity, no discussion possible, so that still needs fixing. Whomever had these two separated should be fired for an utter lack of intelligence and understanding of physics. There are a lot of better ways to fix that imbvalance that causes, and it is more efficient as well, just contact me for details (and credits of course)

No auto-placement, but ANY point. After all, yau are defending, and can deploy forces wherever you see fit. Especially with Antaran attacks, you have 5 turns warning, so REMOVE the FCKN aout-placement, and allow full tactical deployment of ships on the map. This is evidence of hiding poor AI programming, and that the devs are essentially incompetent to provide proper AI.
Later updates of the game have corrected the gravity issue, however it is now most useful to start with a low gravity small homeworld with a 50% production boost and more points wherever you need. These devs seem to utterly fail to grasp the concept of balance, even in a relatively simple game like this, and I am sorry to say my negative review remains negative. What I fail to grasp is that a (presumably) intelligent team can come up with this type of poor balance of the game. Perhaps they should fire some game designers and hire some from Blizzard. I basically gave up playing computer games when I left university 15 years ago. Back then the game was Championship Manager, which I loved.
Nonetheless when I found out about this game I have it a try, as I'm really into the NFL, spreadsheets, statistics, Bill Barnwell columns on ESPN, those sorts of things. Since then the amount of hours I've spent immersed in this game is astonishing. Its analytical depth is amazing; the game engine is a masterpiece.
Many people will do what I did, which is play the game single-player until it becomes too easy to beat the AI (which took a couple of months of solid play), then graduate to the multi-player scene. I'm in a league called the GML which is great fun. There's a devoted, welcoming community of veterans who have been playing this game for 10 years + and still haven't cracked it fully - they often post useful guidance on the FOFC forum. Any new player looking to improve will find plenty to work with there. It's a steep learning curve, but worth it.
If you've got FOF7 the main reasons to migrate to FOF 8 are (1) if you play multi-player, or ever intend to, in which case your league will migrate and (2) if you value the coaching features, such as playbooks and deeper gameplanning, which have been added. The GM side of the game hasn't been updated that much, which is a good thing.

I have been playing this game since the minute it came out. I am a huge fan of harvest moon and I love that game. I could play it to my death bed. And then Stardew Valley came out. I have been playing nothing but this game. It is wonderful. The graphics are exactly what they should be for a harvest moon look-a-like. You have 5 skills, fishing, farming, mining, foraging, and combat. You have 4 seasons and each crop has a specific season to which it grows. You can grow as little or as much as you want within the seasons. You have holidays and plenty of activities that you can do. There is nothing that tells you what you can and cannot do. You want to fish all day then fish. You wake every morning at 6am. and you must be in bed by 2am every day. If you don't get into bed by 2 then you fall asleep where you are standing but it will cost you. You can mine in the mines, and there are 100 levels of rocks, gems and mobs you can attack. The deeper you go the harder the mobs get. You have a full town of people you can interact with. You can marry whomever you choose. If you want to marry a female and you are a female you can, and vice versa with males. There is a bar you can visit, a doctors office, a general store, a carpenter, a blacksmith, and a farmer. Oh! and a library. You have unlimited possibilities in this game and it can go on for as long as you want. Basically you have a world at your fingertips. Do what you will with it. There are quests that will give you money. Some are timed but most are not. You also get a pet in the beginning and it can either be a cat or dog that stays on your farm. You also have plenty of options to basically homestead on your land. Honey making, maple syrup, pine tar, and oak resin. You can also make your own wine, your own cloth, charcoal, jelly's and so much more. I can literally go on and on about this game. I am on my 4th game. I have three different games on my computer, and I have the game on my PS4 which has two saved games on there. I am in love with this game and it has been a perfect game for spending hours on. (I have 297 hours in it on my computer so far).

I have rarely played virtual basketball as I've always preferred to go outside and shoot hoops. This is a review coming from a soccer fanatic who somehow ended up playing this game competitively against his friends almost every weekend. If you're looking for an all around basketball experience, you'll find it here.
NBA 2K16
is quite solid all around. Players who are used to mashing buttons or slide tackling consistently will have a few issues adapting to this playing style as you'll have to be pretty clean to keep the game going. NBA is quite consistent with its fouls and does a pretty good job letting the player feel out how much their pushing into someone else. There are the odd times where the checking will feel weird, but for the most part it is done pretty smoothly (and fairly). Dribbling is quite easy to do and the skill moves can be done with a flick of the right stick. The action around the key is pretty rock solid and the AI seem to do their job covering other players well. Passing is smooth and alleyoops are possible with the right timing. The dunking animations are pretty cool, but not to the extreme levels that NBA Jam provided. You won't be doing 3 back flips with a rainbow jump any time soon! Shots are pretty standard and rely on the player to release the button at a certain time. The left thumb stuck can put some spin or turn on the basketball.The career mode is also quite interactive. If you love the create a star mode with interview questions, press coferences and all that jazz - you will be jumping head over heels. 20 hours of this game was me playing against my friends while the other hours were played by my little brother who would absolutely love sitting through boring press conferences answering questions.
The
and animations are well done. Since I'm an impact, boom boom let's see some instant explosions sort of player, it feels a little slow and sluggish while checking or jumping in the air to make a block. If you are successful in making a block or a check, it can look and feel pretty cool. The
are decent. The crowd does cheer for big moments in the game and the announcers do a pretty good job calling the play. You won't hear much from the players or coaches though.
Overall, the game is good and I would recommend it to hardcore basketball fans. If you're just a regular gamer looking for something different - I would recommend waiting for a solid sale.

With this, the first installment in the
series, Zoom Out Games hit bull's eye upon release in March 2015. The mere fact that only half a year later the fourth game in the series has already been greenlit, speaks tons about the game's success.
is being advertised as a casual strategy game, but in reality it's a time-management game with very limited strategical options or choices. The story, although rooted in Greek mythology, is shallow and serves merely as a framework for the 40-odd levels. These levels are almost all based upon the same principle: control your workers (and now and then a very lazy Hercules or some other mythological figure) in order to clear the path towards the objective. In order to do so, you'll need three resources: food, materials & gold. These can be found or collected in several different ways, such as constructing and upgrading appropriate buildings.
Since each level is timed, it's quite important to take a look at the map before rushing off, noticing the places where buildings can be put or gold can be found. Playing on "casual" difficulty let me progress through the game without much of a hassle, collecting "gold score" on almost every level at the first try (and I am a complete noob at this type of game). But the higher difficulty setting was an entirely different story: all of sudden every second counted, and one wrong action early on in a level could ruin it. An extra difficulty level in between these two extremes would have been nice, but that's a very minor criticism.
During the course of a level, the player can activate one or more "powers" which boost some aspect of the gathering & building process. This provides a neat extra layer of gameplay, something the game needed more and more while progressing since the levels are nearly all built upon the same principle. Happily, the levels are never too long: most of them last somewhere between 5 and 10 minutes, which makes the game perfectly suited to be consumed as a gaming snack.
comes with full Steam integration such as trading cards, leaderboards and a varied bunch of achievements. These are not very difficult but still entertaining, and the game can be completed to 100% really easily or without any tiresome grinding.
